articles.title: Gold price prediction: Despite 27% decline from January peak, UBS still retains  ₹1.50 lakh/10 gram target for 2027
articles.excerpt:
Gold price outlook: Gold prices have suffered a sharp correction from their record highs, but UBS is not backing away from its bullish long-term outlook. UBS Global Wealth Management has retained its forecast of $5,000 per ounce (approximately ₹1.50 lakh per 10 grams) by December 2027, keeping its rating on the precious metal at Attractive.

The forecast stands out as investors reassess the outlook for US interest rates, with a stronger dollar and higher real yields weighing on bullion. Gold has also faced pressure from improved risk appetite in equity markets and liquidity-driven selling. However, UBS believes these near-term headwinds do not undermine the structural reasons to hold gold.

articles.title: India’s gold loan portfolio surges 60.6% to ₹23.3 lakh crore, smaller cities drive growth: Report
articles.excerpt:
Gold loans accounted for 12.6% of India’s ₹185.2 lakh crore retail loan portfolio, marking an increase of 3.3 percentage points from a year earlier.

India's gold loan market continued to expand rapidly, with the outstanding portfolio rising 60.6 per cent year-on-year to ₹23.3 lakh crore, supported by larger loan sizes and growing participation from borrowers in smaller cities, according to a report by CRIF Credit Information Services.

The report said the growth of gold loans is spreading beyond traditional markets in southern India, with Tier III and beyond cities emerging as important contributors.

articles.title: Rupee soars 69 paise to settle at its eight-month high of 92.16 against US dollar

The rupee on Wednesday jumped 69 paise to settle at 92.16 (provisional), the highest level in this year so far, drawing cues from robust buying in domestic equity markets and unabated foreign fund inflows.

Lower crude oil prices also helped the local currency pare all its losses of the current financial year while investors worldwide preferred Indian equities over other assets, forex traders said.
